title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: Chamier — Adam constitutes sinners causally, not formally
pass_a_gloss: Chamier says that constitutes us sinners causally, not formally—more on that in its place. Those were the only OT finds you thought could clinch the charge. Placeus could have stacked great divines behind his answers and mined the same texts for counters; he prefers brevity and will not bury the reader under argument-heaps.
pass_b_english: For that (as most learned Chamier has it) constitutes us sinners not formally, but causally; of which matter in its place. These alone you found in the Old Testament by which you thought that imputation could be concluded. I could also have propped my replies with the authority of great Theologians, and from the same places drawn forth other arguments hostile to yours: but I consult brevity, and I do not wish to weary you as reader with too great a flood of arguments.
source_text: Id enim (ut habet eruditissimus Chamierus) nos peccatores constituit non formaliter, sed causaliter; qua de re suo loco. Haec sola invenisti in vetere Testamento, quibus illam imputationem concludi posse putares. Potuissem & responsiones meas magnorum Theologorum authoritate fulcire, & iisdem ex locis alia argumenta promere tuis infesta: sed consulo brevitatem, & nolo te nimia argumentorum profusione legentem fatigare.

choices.choice: Causal not formal; OT finds exhausted; brevity
